outcome: Endpoint and network activity are correlated into one detection, so affected machines are identified fast enough to keep a line running.
overview: Endpoint and network detections usually live in different tools, which means an analyst sees a suspicious process on a laptop and a suspicious connection at the perimeter as two separate things and has to guess whether they are the same event. Cortex XDR collects both into one data set so the correlation is done for them. In a manufacturing estate the value is concentrated in scoping — knowing quickly which machines were involved is what decides whether a line keeps running while an investigation proceeds.

benefits.text: Endpoint and network activity are correlated into one detection rather than two alerts
benefits.limits: Correlation needs both sources onboarded; endpoint-only deployments get an endpoint product and should be scoped as one

benefits.text: An incident can be scoped across machines quickly, which decides whether production continues
benefits.limits: Scoping depth is bounded by retention purchased; a slow-burning intrusion may predate the window

benefits.text: One agent covers prevention and detection, reducing what has to be deployed to a production endpoint
benefits.limits: The control plane is vendor-operated, so tenant region and log residency are design decisions to be made and recorded explicitly rather than properties of the product

residency: Vendor-operated control plane; endpoint telemetry leaves the customer estate and the tenant region is chosen and recorded at design

notFor.situation: An estate already running another endpoint detection sensor in blocking mode
notFor.why: Two behavioural sensors on one endpoint contend, and attribution of a stall costs more than either saves

notFor.situation: Production terminals whose vendor forbids an additional agent
notFor.why: Support conditions on production equipment outrank a security preference

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to blocking on office classes with network telemetry onboarded
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed detection with an agreed response target.
1) Discovery — endpoint inventory by class, agent conflicts, vendor constraints, scoping-time baseline
2) Design — machine classes, per-class policy, rings, containment authorisation and telemetry sources
3) Roll out — agents deployed ring by ring in detection-only mode, network telemetry onboarded
4) Enable and hand over — blocking per class after a measured period, operations handed over

A scoping query returns the affected machine set inside the agreed time
Every class moved to blocking has a recorded owner sign-off
